problem: A trial with a frozen preference encoder typically predicts on a held batch, reports fitting predictions and asks for held probabilities. The GTE preference path used a separate call that bypassed the ordinary worker's existing two-batch frozen feature reuse. Thus it could pay twice to encode exactly the same held texts within one trial.
change: Use the existing verified sentence encoder batch function for these same mean-pooled encoders. Reuse applies only when already enabled by the worker, with the same pinned weight path, tokenization length, pooling, prefix and ordered unique texts. The existing bound and class/metric behavior remain in force. No model identifiers affect scheduling, training labels are never cached and no evaluation labels are opened.
experiment: Use the actual frozen primary component chosen as the 710 model's adviser source. Draw two fixed pairs of fitting/held batches solely from the original training data, with held sizes 96 and 192 and fit sizes twice that. Compare reuse off/on for the first and on/off for the second, clearing the batch cache at every switch and warming both modes on unrelated rows. Exercise the real predictor and class probabilities in the same order as a training worker. Check exact predictions on both roles and exact probabilities on held rows. Count real frozen encoder invocations and observe wall and CPU times.
accept: At both sizes require byte-identical outputs, one fewer actual encoder invocation and lower process CPU use. Report wall separately under concurrent load. A success is a scoped speed improvement only, not a score gain or a measured increase in the number of candidates the whole agent can afford. Zero local supervised fits or model API calls. No designated validation, official test or H2.
